title: What Is Your Dog Actually Saying With That Side-Eye?
description:
It has a real name, and it's not sass — it's your dog asking for space.

script: That look where your dog's head stays completely still but their eyes swivel over to you, showing a crescent of white, has an actual name in animal behavior science, it's called whale eye. And it's not sass or attitude the way it often gets joked about online, it's a genuine stress signal. Dogs give whale eye when they want something to stop or want more space, but don't feel the need to escalate to growling or moving away yet, it's an early, quiet warning sign. You'll often see it around resource guarding, uncomfortable hugs, or unfamiliar dogs getting too close too fast. The reason this actually matters is that whale eye is one of the clearest early signals before things escalate, dogs that get ignored at this stage sometimes have to move to a growl or a snap just to be heard. So if you catch that side-eye, the smart move is to just give a little space. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
